rituals.goal: Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.mission: Catch the instant an unchosen thought begins.
rituals.play: Rest on one neutral point. When a thought appears by itself, catch only its first instant before following it.
rituals.twist: Classify only its form—word, image, memory, plan, sensation—then release.
rituals.win: You notice an arrival before it becomes a complete thought.
rituals.mindBend: A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.
rituals.mind_bend: A spontaneous thought has a beginning you can catch, separating the arrival of mental content from the act of choosing it.
rituals.safety: Use only one ordinary thought. If forced mental blankness appears, stop and look at a physical object nearby.

rituals.mission: Let only word one enter the round.

rituals.goal: Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.mission: Allow thought one but deny it a sequel.
rituals.rule: The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.one_rule: The first thought is permitted in full.
rituals.play: Let one thought finish. For the next five seconds, any explanation, defence, prediction or replay counts as a sequel and gets no continuation.
rituals.twist: A genuinely unrelated thought may enter.
rituals.win: The original thought ends without becoming a chain.
rituals.mindBend: The first thought and its explanatory sequel are separate events; rumination begins in what gets added after the thought is already complete.
rituals.mind_bend: The first thought and its explanatory sequel are separate events; rumination begins in what gets added after the thought is already complete.
rituals.safety: Keep this to everyday mental content. When compulsive thought monitoring appears, step out and move back to everyday activity.

rituals.name: QUEUE MASTER
rituals.unique_game_move: serialize simultaneous thought arrivals
rituals.recognition_cue: Mental overload. ROUTER TAGS: overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load
rituals.immediate_need: reduce what the mind has to hold at once
rituals.match_reason: Mental overload; THOUGHT STREAM; ROUTER TAGS: overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load overwhelmed overload too much busy mind working memory mental load
rituals.goal: Force multiple arrivals into a one-at-a-time queue.
rituals.mission: Force multiple arrivals into a one-at-a-time queue.
rituals.rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.one_rule: Only one item can occupy the front slot.
rituals.play: When several thoughts compete, imagine numbered tickets. Process only the lowest number for three beats; all others wait silently.
rituals.twist: After three beats, move the front ticket to the back without solving it.
rituals.win: Competition becomes an orderly sequence rather than a pile-up.
rituals.mindBend: Mental overload can come from simultaneous competition, not sheer quantity; sequencing the arrivals changes the pressure without deleting any of them.
rituals.mind_bend: Mental overload can come from simultaneous competition, not sheer quantity; sequencing the arrivals changes the pressure without deleting any of them.
rituals.safety: Choose everyday mental content. When greater thought preoccupation appears, end the round; do something simple and concrete.

rituals.goal: Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.mission: Pop only the newest item from awareness.
rituals.play: When several thoughts are active, identify the one that arrived last. Let only that newest item fade or leave; do nothing to earlier items.
rituals.twist: Repeat once only if another clear newest item exists.
rituals.win: You experience mental load decreasing by last-in-first-out removal.
rituals.mindBend: The newest mental item can be released while older material remains. Relief does not always require solving the oldest issue first.
rituals.mind_bend: The newest mental item can be released while older material remains. Relief does not always require solving the oldest issue first.
rituals.safety: Work only with a brief thought sample for one pass. If forced mental blankness develops, pause the exercise and allow the mind to continue without forcing it.

rituals.name: LOOP COUNTER
rituals.unique_game_move: measure whether repetition adds new information
rituals.recognition_cue: Rumination. ROUTER TAGS: replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping
rituals.immediate_need: interrupt replay and unhook from the loop
rituals.match_reason: Rumination; THOUGHT STREAM; ROUTER TAGS: replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping replay replaying rumination ruminating regret past memory looping
rituals.goal: Count loops only when the same mental job repeats.
rituals.mission: Count loops only when the same mental job repeats.
rituals.rule: Wording changes do not create a new loop.
rituals.one_rule: Wording changes do not create a new loop.
rituals.play: Each time the mind revisits the issue, score +1 only if it adds no new fact, decision or action.

Catch how long a cue takes to produce a thought.

ONE RULE
Use a neutral cue.

PLAY
Look at a neutral word such as TREE. Notice the first associated thought and estimate whether it came instantly, after one beat, or later.

TWIST
One trial only.

WIN
Cue-to-thought delay becomes perceptible.

There is measurable space between a cue and the mind’s response, so reaction can have latency even when it feels instantaneous.

SAFETY
For one pass, use a brief thought sample. When compulsive thought monitoring appears, stop at that point and resume what you were doing.

rituals.goal: Stretch the most loaded word into slow syllables.

rituals.safety: Make this a brief exercise with manageable inner wording. When compulsive sentence repetition appears, stop at that point and let the sentence alone remain as it is.

display.fullRitual:
GAME
TWO-SENSE SPLIT

GOAL
Hold cross-modal divided attention.

ONE RULE
One cue per sense.

PLAY
View one neutral object while simultaneously noticing one background sound.

TWIST
Five seconds — end two-sense split.

WIN
Two sensory channels can share awareness without merging.

MIND BEND
A sight and a sound can share awareness simultaneously. Attention may coordinate across sensory channels instead of operating as one single-track beam.

SAFETY
Use comfortable visual attention for this pass. When eye strain or headache appears, end it there and turn to a practical task nearby.

rituals.goal: Make straight horizontal lines look slanted using staggered tiles.
rituals.mission: Make straight horizontal lines look slanted using staggered tiles.
rituals.rule: The mortar lines remain perfectly parallel and horizontal.
rituals.one_rule: The mortar lines remain perfectly parallel and horizontal.
rituals.play: Picture two rows of alternating black/white tiles. Offset the second row by half a tile and place a thin grey horizontal line between rows. Notice whether the line appears slightly tilted or stepped.
rituals.twist: Reveal that the separator is straight only after the first impression.

rituals.mindBend: Straight parallel lines can look tilted because of surrounding tile offsets. Visual context is powerful enough to distort an apparently simple geometric judgement.

rituals.safety: Use content that stays clearly manageable for this pass. If flashback-like imagery appears, leave the round and shift back to visible surroundings.

display.mindBend: A digit can be odd in value while occupying an even position. The unchanged symbol can carry independent classifications at once.
display.safety: Choose comfortable visual attention. When compulsive focus checking becomes noticeable, step out and release the attentional effort.
display.fullRitual:
GAME
DIGIT PARITY SORT

GOAL
Turn one number into two different parity patterns.

ONE RULE
Use a three- or four-digit neutral number.

PLAY
Take 5724. First tag each digit odd/even by value, then separately tag each position odd/even.

TWIST
Do not calculate the total.

WIN
The same number supports two nonspatial classification systems.

MIND BEND
A digit can be odd in value while occupying an even position. The unchanged symbol can carry independent classifications at once.

SAFETY
Choose comfortable visual attention. When compulsive focus checking becomes noticeable, step out and release the attentional effort.

rituals.goal: See how much a cue rescues memory.
rituals.mission: See how much a cue rescues memory.
rituals.play: Study: MAP, CLOUD, KEY, APPLE, TRAIN. After a five-second pause, freely recall what you can. Then inspect MAP, RIVER, KEY, APPLE, CHAIR, TRAIN, CLOUD and mark which were on the original list.

rituals.goal: Expose sequence uncertainty instead of comparing temporal distance.
rituals.mission: Expose sequence uncertainty instead of comparing temporal distance.
rituals.play: Recall a short mild sequence and mark the one transition whose order you are least sure about.
rituals.twist: Do not reconstruct the missing order.
rituals.win: You can identify the exact point where the remembered sequence stops feeling certain.
rituals.mindBend: Uncertainty about sequence can belong to one specific gap rather than the whole memory, separating a local ordering failure from total unreliability.
rituals.mind_bend: Uncertainty about sequence can belong to one specific gap rather than the whole memory, separating a local ordering failure from total unreliability.
rituals.safety: Choose only one mild memory. When emotional flooding appears, end the round; contact someone safe or a clinician.

rituals.fullRitual:
GAME
MEMORY SEQUENCE HOLE

GOAL
Expose sequence uncertainty instead of comparing temporal distance.

ONE RULE
One gap only.

PLAY
Recall a short mild sequence and mark the one transition whose order you are least sure about.

TWIST
Do not reconstruct the missing order.

WIN
You can identify the exact point where the remembered sequence stops feeling certain.

MIND BEND
Uncertainty about sequence can belong to one specific gap rather than the whole memory, separating a local ordering failure from total unreliability.

SAFETY
Choose only one mild memory. When emotional flooding appears, end the round; contact someone safe or a clinician.

rituals.goal: Use one new category.
rituals.mission: Use one new category.
rituals.rule: Choose categories like lesson, warning, transition, ordinary event, unfinished issue.
rituals.one_rule: Choose categories like lesson, warning, transition, ordinary event, unfinished issue.

rituals.goal: Test whether generating part of an answer changes memory.
rituals.mission: Test whether generating part of an answer changes memory.
rituals.rule: One item is completed by you; one is simply given.
rituals.one_rule: One item is completed by you; one is simply given.

rituals.goal: Find where one remembered event naturally becomes another.
rituals.mission: Find where one remembered event naturally becomes another.
rituals.rule: Use a real context change, not an arbitrary time length.
rituals.one_rule: Use a real context change, not an arbitrary time length.
rituals.play: Recall a mild recent sequence and locate the first clear shift in place, goal or activity—such as leaving the car and entering the shop. Treat that shift as the event boundary.
rituals.twist: Do not replay details on both sides once the boundary is found.
rituals.win: Memory becomes segmented by event structure rather than by an imposed time window.
rituals.mindBend: A remembered episode naturally breaks where goal, place or activity changes. Event boundaries are context shifts rather than arbitrary slices of clock time.
rituals.mind_bend: A remembered episode naturally breaks where goal, place or activity changes. Event boundaries are context shifts rather than arbitrary slices of clock time.
rituals.safety: Keep the round within a mild image or thought for one pass. Do not continue if loss of present orientation develops; leave the memory alone.

rituals.goal: Jump ten days forward on a seven-day week.
rituals.mission: Jump ten days forward on a seven-day week.
rituals.rule: After Sunday, wrap back to Monday.

rituals.name: ARROW-LINE ILLUSION
rituals.unique_game_move: compare two equal imagined line segments whose surrounding arrowhead context biases apparent length
rituals.recognition_cue: Mental imagery • Visual play. ROUTER TAGS: image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene
rituals.immediate_need: shift the mental image without forcing it away
rituals.match_reason: Mental imagery • Visual play; IMAGE GEOMETRY; ROUTER TAGS: image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene image imagery visual picture mental movie movie flashback scene
rituals.goal: Test whether context can bend apparent size.
rituals.mission: Test whether context can bend apparent size.
rituals.rule: The two central lines are exactly equal.
rituals.one_rule: The two central lines are exactly equal.
rituals.play: Picture two equal horizontal lines. Put inward-pointing arrowheads on the first (>—<) and outward-pointing arrowheads on the second (<—>). Notice which central line feels longer before reminding yourself they are equal.
rituals.twist: Judge the central lines, not the full arrow shapes.
rituals.win: Context changes apparent length even though the central line lengths were held equal.
rituals.mindBend: Arrowheads can distort where the endpoints of an equal line seem to sit. Apparent length is an interpretation of boundary context rather than the central segment alone.
rituals.mind_bend: Arrowheads can distort where the endpoints of an equal line seem to sit. Apparent length is an interpretation of boundary context rather than the central segment alone.
rituals.safety: Use only a mild image or thought. When greater vividness or fear appears, leave the exercise; open your eyes and take in the room.

rituals.rule: Both examples must genuinely belong to the category.
rituals.one_rule: Both examples must genuinely belong to the category.

rituals.rule: Two or three ON inputs produce ON; zero or one produce OFF.

display.fullRitual:
GAME
BARGAIN LABEL

GOAL
Catch negotiation before compliance.

ONE RULE
One label only.

PLAY
When the mind says 'just once', 'later I'll stop', or similar, label BARGAIN and do not answer it.

TWIST
Return to chosen action.

WIN
Bargaining is recognized as a process rather than a decision.

MIND BEND
The first bargaining sentence marks the moment an urge recruits reasoning on its behalf. Negotiation is a stage of the impulse rather than neutral analysis.

SAFETY
Work only with a manageable low-risk urge. If rising danger or loss of control appears, do not continue; seek immediate human support.

rituals.recognition_cue: Body awareness • Grounding. ROUTER TAGS: focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor focus distracted attention grounding present restless mental quiet anchor
rituals.immediate_need: steady attention and return to the present

rituals.goal: Make one hand feel mentally larger without moving it.
rituals.mission: Make one hand feel mentally larger without moving it.
rituals.rule: Keep the real hand visible and still.
rituals.one_rule: Keep the real hand visible and still.
rituals.play: Look at one relaxed hand. For three seconds imagine its felt outline extending slightly beyond the real edges, then compare imagined and visible boundaries.
rituals.twist: Use only a small change; stop if it feels unsettling.
rituals.win: The body-image boundary and the visible hand can be noticed as separate representations.
rituals.mindBend: An imagined hand can briefly feel visually larger while the real hand remains unchanged. Body-size representation is editable rather than a perfect copy of physical reality.
rituals.mind_bend: An imagined hand can briefly feel visually larger while the real hand remains unchanged. Body-size representation is editable rather than a perfect copy of physical reality.
rituals.safety: Keep this to a comfortable, harmless visual-body illusion. If concerning physical symptoms arise, abandon the exercise and seek appropriate medical assessment rather than using the illusion or attention shift as reassurance.

rituals.goal: Catch a streak trying to rewrite probability.
rituals.mission: Catch a streak trying to rewrite probability.
rituals.rule: Every fair coin flip remains independent.
rituals.one_rule: Every fair coin flip remains independent.
rituals.play: Imagine five fair-coin results: H-H-H-H-H. Before the sixth flip, notice whether TAILS feels 'due.' Then state the actual probability of tails on flip six.
rituals.twist: Do not average across the six flips; judge only the next one.
rituals.win: A streak-induced expectation separates from the unchanged 50/50 next-flip probability.
rituals.mindBend: A streak of identical coin outcomes does not alter the next fair flip. One implication is the mind’s tendency to mistake recent sequence for a change in independent probability.
rituals.mind_bend: A streak of identical coin outcomes does not alter the next fair flip. One implication is the mind’s tendency to mistake recent sequence for a change in independent probability.
rituals.safety: Work only with a low-stakes mental game. If self-judgment from frustration becomes noticeable, pause the exercise and move on without forcing a solution.

ROLE-NAME MEMORY

GOAL
Give the same word two roles and see which one memory remembers better.

ONE RULE
The label stays identical; only its role changes.

PLAY
Imagine one person introduced as 'Baker'—a surname. Imagine another described as 'a baker'—the profession. After five seconds, recall everything you can about each.

TWIST
Do not add extra facts deliberately.

WIN
Meaningful role context changes what the same verbal label makes memorable.

MIND BEND

Use one self-judged set and one meaning-judged set.

PLAY

TWIST
Do not rehearse the words after judging them.

WIN
Self-referential encoding can leave a different memory trace from ordinary semantic encoding.

MIND BEND
Neutral words judged in relation to the self can be remembered differently from words processed only for meaning. Self-reference is a powerful encoding cue.

SAFETY
Restrict the exercise to manageable identity material. If global self-condemnation appears, stop the exercise; shift back to specific facts.

rituals.goal: Move the finish line closer without changing the next step.
rituals.mission: Move the finish line closer without changing the next step.
rituals.rule: The next required action is unchanged across the two rounds.
rituals.one_rule: The next required action is unchanged across the two rounds.

rituals.twist: Do not change reward, difficulty or time—only apparent progress.
rituals.win: Proximity to completion can change motivational pull while the next action remains identical.
rituals.mindBend: The same next action can feel easier when imagined near the finish than near the start. Apparent progress itself is an origin of motivational pull.
rituals.mind_bend: The same next action can feel easier when imagined near the finish than near the start. Apparent progress itself is an origin of motivational pull.
rituals.safety: Work only with a safe ordinary task. Rest or reassess the priority when the exercise shifts into pushing through illness or exhaustion; do not continue the task.

rituals.goal: Find the winning first move from seven tokens.
rituals.mission: Find the winning first move from seven tokens.
rituals.rule: Each player may remove 1, 2, or 3 tokens; whoever takes the last token wins.
rituals.one_rule: Each player may remove 1, 2, or 3 tokens; whoever takes the last token wins.
rituals.play: Imagine a pile of 7 tokens. Choose how many to take first so that whatever the opponent removes, you can force the final token.

rituals.mindBend: In the take-away game, leaving a multiple of four controls the opponent’s possibilities. An invariant is a strategy stronger than guessing individual moves.

rituals.name: GRAPH COLOURING
rituals.unique_game_move: assign colours to connected nodes so adjacent nodes never share a colour while using as few colours as possible

rituals.goal: Colour a tiny network without neighbours matching.
rituals.mission: Colour a tiny network without neighbours matching.
rituals.play: Picture a triangle A-B-C-A. Assign colours to A B plus C while minimising the number of colours.
rituals.twist: Then add node D connected only to A and ask whether a new colour is needed.
rituals.win: Constraint structure determines the minimum number of categories required.
rituals.mindBend: A graph can be coloured with minimal colours by obeying only adjacency constraints. Global efficiency is the result of many local incompatibility rules.
rituals.mind_bend: A graph can be coloured with minimal colours by obeying only adjacency constraints. Global efficiency is the result of many local incompatibility rules.
rituals.safety: Keep this as a brief, low-stakes logic puzzle. If frustration becomes self-judgment or you start repeating the same search, stop and leave the colouring problem unfinished.

rituals.goal: Lock one pleasant thing to one avoided task.
rituals.mission: Lock one pleasant thing to one avoided task.
rituals.rule: The pleasant item is available only while doing the target task.
rituals.one_rule: The pleasant item is available only while doing the target task.
rituals.play: Choose a harmless treat such as a favourite playlist. Mentally set the rule: playlist ON only while doing the first ten minutes of the avoided task; playlist OFF when the task stops.
rituals.twist: Do not give yourself the reward in advance.
rituals.win: Task entry gains an immediate reward without requiring motivation to appear first.
rituals.mindBend: Making an immediate pleasure available only during a less-attractive task turns reward timing into a controllable contingency that supports engagement.
rituals.mind_bend: Making an immediate pleasure available only during a less-attractive task turns reward timing into a controllable contingency that supports engagement.
rituals.safety: Limit this to one genuinely small action. If compulsive productivity appears, do not continue; rest or reassess the priority.

rituals.goal: Find the middle of time without numbers.
rituals.mission: Find the middle of time without numbers.
rituals.rule: No counting, tapping or breath counting.
rituals.one_rule: No counting, tapping or breath counting.

rituals.twist: Do one trial only; accuracy is not the point.
rituals.win: You experience a subjective midpoint generated without explicit counting.
rituals.mindBend: A rough midpoint can be sensed even without a clock. This reveals an internal sense of duration that can operate when explicit timing tools are removed.

rituals.safety: Keep the interval brief and comfortable. If frustrating repetition develops, stop the exercise and return to ordinary activity.

rituals.goal: Launch two rhythms together and watch them separate.
rituals.mission: Launch two rhythms together and watch them separate.
rituals.rule: The rhythms must have different cycle lengths.
rituals.one_rule: The rhythms must have different cycle lengths.
rituals.play: Run a three-beat pattern and a four-beat pattern together in imagination. Notice the first moment their accents stop landing together.
rituals.twist: End at the first clear drift.
rituals.win: Two internally generated time patterns can be felt as synchronised, then desynchronised.
rituals.mindBend: Two rhythms with different cycle lengths can begin together and naturally separate. Synchrony is a temporary relationship between periods instead of a permanent property.
rituals.mind_bend: Two rhythms with different cycle lengths can begin together and naturally separate. Synchrony is a temporary relationship between periods instead of a permanent property.
rituals.safety: Choose natural unforced breathing. When compulsive counting appears, end the round; let the pattern go.

display.mindBend: A number can be repeatedly transformed down to its digital root while the starting number is still retained. What changes is simultaneous processing and storage demands in working memory.
display.safety: Use harmless puzzle material for this pass. When the exercise shifts into self-judgment from frustration, stop and let the answer remain unresolved.
display.fullRitual:
GAME
DIGITAL ROOT VAULT

GOAL
Compress a number to one digit without losing the original.

ONE RULE
Keep the starting number available.

PLAY
Use a number such as 5724. Sum its digits, then sum again if needed until one digit remains; afterward recall 5724 exactly.

TWIST
Do not write anything down.

WIN
A derived one-digit result is computed while the original number remains retrievable.

MIND BEND
A number can be repeatedly transformed down to its digital root while the starting number is still retained. What changes is simultaneous processing and storage demands in working memory.

SAFETY
Use harmless puzzle material for this pass. When the exercise shifts into self-judgment from frustration, stop and let the answer remain unresolved.

rituals.goal: Catch whether one code carries a valid built-in check.
rituals.mission: Catch whether one code carries a valid built-in check.
rituals.rule: Check digit equals the last digit of the sum of the earlier digits.
rituals.one_rule: Check digit equals the last digit of the sum of the earlier digits.
rituals.play: Test code 4723: add 4+7+2=13, take the last digit 3, and compare it with the final digit.

rituals.mindBend: A check digit adds redundant structure that can expose a mismatch in a code. This explains how verification can be built into information rather than relying on memory confidence.

rituals.goal: Hide one oddball in a list and see what memory keeps.
rituals.mission: Hide one oddball in a list and see what memory keeps.
rituals.rule: One item must differ sharply from the rest.
rituals.one_rule: One item must differ sharply from the rest.
rituals.play: Hold this list once: chair, table, lamp, TIGER, sofa, desk. After five seconds, freely recall as many items as you can.
rituals.twist: Notice where TIGER appears in recall; do not deliberately rehearse it.
rituals.win: A distinctive item competes differently for memory than ordinary neighbours.
rituals.mindBend: One distinctive item can stand out in later recall simply because it differed sharply from its neighbours. Contrast is an encoding advantage.
rituals.mind_bend: One distinctive item can stand out in later recall simply because it differed sharply from its neighbours. Contrast is an encoding advantage.
rituals.safety: Limit the material to a small memory load. If compulsive rehearsal appears, leave the round and release the items.

rituals.goal: Use a finite checking blackout.
rituals.mission: Use a finite checking blackout.
rituals.play: Place a token marked NO CHECK for e.g. ten minutes or one task segment.
rituals.twist: Do not ask/search/check until token expires.
rituals.win: Checking becomes a choice with a boundary.
rituals.mindBend: A short no-check interval can be precommitted and completed without obtaining reassurance. The checking impulse and actual checking behaviour are separable.

rituals.safety: Use the no-check interval only for ordinary, nonurgent doubt. If the uncertainty becomes frightening or hard to verify, stop solo checking and bring the situation to a trusted person, clinician, or other reliable external source before acting on it.

rituals.goal: Prove you understood the answer by teaching it back.

rituals.one_rule: Use your own wording without adding new information.
rituals.play: Take a simple answer such as 'The appointment moved from 2pm to 3pm.' Restate it from memory using different wording, then compare against the original fact.

rituals.win: Understanding is checked through accurate reconstruction rather than repeated questioning.
rituals.mindBend: Restating information in your own words can expose a changed time, condition or qualifier. Comprehension is something testable beyond the feeling of understanding.

rituals.safety: Choose one unresolved question. When frightening unverifiable uncertainty appears, end the round; connect with someone who can support you.

rituals.goal: Ask the question that cuts uncertainty closest to half.
rituals.mission: Ask the question that cuts uncertainty closest to half.
rituals.play: Imagine eight possible cards numbered 1–8. Compare asking 'Is it even?' with 'Is it greater than 7?' Decide which question would eliminate more possibilities regardless of the answer.
rituals.twist: Judge the split, not which answer you hope for.
rituals.win: A well-chosen question reduces uncertainty by dividing possibilities efficiently.
rituals.mindBend: A yes-no question removes the most uncertainty when it divides possibilities as evenly as possible, making information gain a feature of the split—not of the answer you hope for.
rituals.mind_bend: A yes-no question removes the most uncertainty when it divides possibilities as evenly as possible, making information gain a feature of the split—not of the answer you hope for.
rituals.safety: Use a question that can stay open for this pass. When doubt starts moving to new questions, step out and let someone safe know what is happening.

rituals.mission: Use external verification for destabilizing uncertainty.
rituals.rule: Do not act on frightening interpretation alone.

rituals.mindBend: A frightening interpretation that is hard to verify belongs in shared reality with another person. External checking is a safety tool when solitary certainty is unreliable.

rituals.goal: See whether your own choice quietly becomes your population estimate.
rituals.mission: See whether your own choice quietly becomes your population estimate.
rituals.rule: Preference and prevalence are two separate answers.
rituals.one_rule: Preference and prevalence are two separate answers.
rituals.play: Choose tea or coffee. Then estimate, out of 100 random adults, how many would make the same choice. Notice whether your own preference pulls the estimate upward.
rituals.twist: Keep the population estimate separate from whether your own choice is better.
rituals.win: Personal preference and assumed social prevalence become distinct judgements.
rituals.mindBend: Personal preference can inflate estimates of how many other people agree. False consensus is projection from ‘I choose this’ to ‘most people probably would too’.
rituals.mind_bend: Personal preference can inflate estimates of how many other people agree. False consensus is projection from ‘I choose this’ to ‘most people probably would too’.
rituals.safety: Use a trivial preference with no social stakes. If the estimate starts feeding certainty about what other people think or becomes a self-worth comparison, stop and return to observable facts.

OLD GOAL EXTRACT

GOAL
Keep direction, discard destination.

ONE RULE
One underlying value.

PLAY
Take an outdated goal and ask what it was trying to serve—security, creativity, contribution, mastery, freedom.

TWIST
Retain value only.

WIN
Meaning can survive a dead goal.

MIND BEND
A goal can stop fitting while the value underneath it remains alive. Values are portable motives that can survive the death of one particular plan.

SAFETY
For this round, choose meaning that can remain uncertain. If forced positivity appears, finish there and go back to concrete reality.

rituals.goal: Keep what belongs to A but not B.
rituals.mission: Keep what belongs to A but not B.
rituals.play: Imagine A={apple, pear, plum} and B={pear, plum, peach}. State A minus B without listing the shared items.
rituals.twist: Then reverse the direction once and state B minus A.
rituals.win: Directional set difference becomes distinct from simple category membership.
rituals.mindBend: Subtracting one set from another produces a different remainder when the direction is reversed. The operation is directional rather than a generic list of what the sets do not share.
rituals.mind_bend: Subtracting one set from another produces a different remainder when the direction is reversed. The operation is directional rather than a generic list of what the sets do not share.
rituals.safety: Use a low-stakes mental game. Move on without rating yourself when perfection pressure shows up; do not continue the task.

rituals.goal: Move a three-disk tower across the pegs.
rituals.mission: Move a three-disk tower across the pegs.
rituals.rule: Only one disk moves at a time; large never sits on small.
rituals.one_rule: Only one disk moves at a time; large never sits on small.

rituals.safety: Use only neutral examples. If perfection pressure shows up, leave the round and move attention into a normal activity.

rituals.goal: Make separate sounds snap into one word.
rituals.mission: Make separate sounds snap into one word.
rituals.rule: Keep the three sounds distinct until the blend.
rituals.one_rule: Keep the three sounds distinct until the blend.
rituals.play: Hear /k/ ... /a/ ... /t/ separately in inner speech. Then shorten the gaps until the three sounds fuse into CAT.
rituals.twist: Do not add any extra sound between them.
rituals.win: Three separate phonemes become one recognised word through temporal blending.
rituals.mindBend: Separate speech sounds can fuse into a single word percept without any sound being changed. Lexical meaning is an emergent result of ordered phoneme combination.
rituals.mind_bend: Separate speech sounds can fuse into a single word percept without any sound being changed. Lexical meaning is an emergent result of ordered phoneme combination.
rituals.safety: Work only with manageable inner wording for one pass. If compulsive sentence repetition develops, stop the exercise; use external text as the reference.

rituals.goal: Move a dot using knight moves only.
rituals.mission: Move a dot using knight moves only.
rituals.rule: Every move is two squares one way and one square sideways.
rituals.one_rule: Every move is two squares one way and one square sideways.
rituals.play: Picture a 5×5 grid with a dot in the centre. Make three legal knight moves, keeping only the dot's current square in mind.
rituals.twist: Do not trace a continuous path between squares.
rituals.win: Position changes through a discrete movement rule rather than continuous attention tracking.
rituals.mindBend: A chess knight changes grid position by a discrete L-shaped rule without travelling through the intervening squares, separating legal state transition from continuous path.
rituals.mind_bend: A chess knight changes grid position by a discrete L-shaped rule without travelling through the intervening squares, separating legal state transition from continuous path.
rituals.safety: Choose harmless puzzle material. If frustration turns into self-judgment, stop without rating your performance.

rituals.name: MEANING MELT
rituals.unique_game_move: repeat one neutral word rapidly until its familiar meaning temporarily weakens and its sound-form becomes more salient

rituals.goal: Repeat a word until it starts sounding strangely like sound.
rituals.mission: Repeat a word until it starts sounding strangely like sound.
rituals.rule: Use one neutral word and keep the pace steady.
rituals.one_rule: Use one neutral word and keep the pace steady.
rituals.play: Pick the neutral word WINDOW. Repeat it internally around fifteen times at a quick, even pace. When the repetitions end, check whether the sound briefly feels stranger than its meaning.
rituals.twist: Avoid explaining the word while repeating it.
rituals.win: A familiar word can momentarily feel like raw sound after sustained repetition.
rituals.mindBend: Rapid repetition can make a familiar neutral word temporarily sound strange and less meaningful. Meaning is an effect that can weaken while the sound-form stays constant.
rituals.mind_bend: Rapid repetition can make a familiar neutral word temporarily sound strange and less meaningful. Meaning is an effect that can weaken while the sound-form stays constant.
rituals.safety: Choose manageable inner wording. When compulsive sentence repetition becomes noticeable, step out and leave the sentence alone.

rituals.goal: Make processing ease change while meaning stays fixed.
rituals.mission: Make processing ease change while meaning stays fixed.
rituals.rule: The sentence text is identical in both rounds.
rituals.one_rule: The sentence text is identical in both rounds.
rituals.play: Use 'Regular sleep supports attention.' First picture it in clear ordinary text; then picture the exact sentence in cramped faint lettering. Compare how immediately convincing or familiar it feels.
rituals.twist: Do not use readability as evidence for truth.
rituals.win: Processing fluency can shift confidence even when the proposition is unchanged.
rituals.mindBend: An identical statement can feel more credible when it is easier to process. Processing fluency is a confidence bias rather than evidence of truth.
rituals.mind_bend: An identical statement can feel more credible when it is easier to process. Processing fluency is a confidence bias rather than evidence of truth.
rituals.safety: Use a small question about what matters for this pass. When forced positivity becomes noticeable, end the round; allow the difficult feeling.

rituals.goal: Fill one missing maths operator.
rituals.mission: Fill one missing maths operator.
rituals.play: Solve 6 ? 3 = 2 by choosing exactly one of +, −, ×, ÷ for the missing slot.
rituals.twist: Check the three wrong operators mentally after choosing.
rituals.win: Division is selected because it is the only operator that satisfies the unchanged equation.
rituals.mindBend: With every number fixed, only the correct operator can make the equation true. Arithmetic meaning is a relationship created by the operation between unchanged values.
rituals.mind_bend: With every number fixed, only the correct operator can make the equation true. Arithmetic meaning is a relationship created by the operation between unchanged values.
rituals.safety: Limit the task to neutral examples for one pass. If proof-seeking repetition develops: walk away without solving it. Leave the exercise there.

rituals.goal: See whether harder recall changes confidence even when more evidence is produced.
rituals.mission: See whether harder recall changes confidence even when more evidence is produced.
rituals.rule: Use the same topic for both rounds.
rituals.one_rule: Use the same topic for both rounds.

rituals.goal: Hear what a sound feels like instead of what made it.
rituals.mission: Hear what a sound feels like instead of what made it.
rituals.play: Choose one real background sound. Decide whether it feels smooth, grainy, pulsing, continuous, sharp, soft-edged, or mixed.
rituals.twist: Keep your eyes on the room and avoid guessing what caused the sound.
rituals.win: Acoustic texture becomes noticeable independently from source meaning.
rituals.mindBend: A sound can be described as rough, smooth, pulsing or continuous without naming its source, separating acoustic texture from the story of what caused it.
rituals.mind_bend: A sound can be described as rough, smooth, pulsing or continuous without naming its source, separating acoustic texture from the story of what caused it.
rituals.safety: Keep this to stable external cues. If reduced physical steadiness appears, end there; let visual attention become natural again.

rituals.goal: See whether similar-sounding words tangle memory.
rituals.mission: See whether similar-sounding words tangle memory.
rituals.rule: Both lists contain the same number of items.
rituals.one_rule: Both lists contain the same number of items.
rituals.play: Hold CAT, MAT, HAT, BAT and recall them. Reset. Hold DOG, SUN, KEY, MAP and recall them. Compare which list was easier to keep distinct.
rituals.twist: Do not build stories linking the words.
rituals.win: Sound similarity can interfere with short-term verbal memory even when list length is unchanged.
rituals.mindBend: Similar-sounding words may be harder to hold in immediate memory than equally long distinct-sounding words. Sound overlap creates interference inside the verbal buffer.
rituals.mind_bend: Similar-sounding words may be harder to hold in immediate memory than equally long distinct-sounding words. Sound overlap creates interference inside the verbal buffer.
rituals.safety: Use one short word-list comparison only. If you start repeatedly retesting yourself or turning recall into a performance score, stop and move to an ordinary task.

No deliberate target selection.

One drift only.

rituals.goal: Give the same object two ownership states and compare value.
rituals.mission: Give the same object two ownership states and compare value.
rituals.rule: The object itself cannot improve or worsen.
rituals.one_rule: The object itself cannot improve or worsen.
rituals.play: Imagine a plain mug is already yours: what minimum price would make you give it up? Reset and imagine it belongs to someone else: what maximum price would you pay for it?

rituals.mindBend: The same neutral mug can feel more valuable when imagined as already owned than when imagined as something to buy. Ownership is a valuation bias.
rituals.mind_bend: The same neutral mug can feel more valuable when imagined as already owned than when imagined as something to buy. Ownership is a valuation bias.
rituals.safety: Limit this to gentle low-effort settling for one pass. When more wakefulness or frustration develops, leave the exercise; let rest be enough.

Decide whether new information should make you stay or switch.

ONE RULE
The host always reveals a losing door you did not choose.

PLAY
Pick Door 1 from three doors. The host, who knows the prize, opens Door 3 and shows no prize. Decide whether to stay with Door 1 or switch to Door 2.

TWIST
Track where the original 2/3 probability mass can go after the host's forced reveal.

WIN
Switching captures the original probability carried by the two unchosen doors and wins with probability 2/3.

MIND BEND
When the host is forced to reveal a losing door, the original two-thirds probability does not vanish; it concentrates on the remaining unchosen door, making switching rational.

SAFETY
Keep this to ordinary low-stakes evidence. When frightening unverifiable interpretations appear, step out and use external verification.

rituals.goal: Count the invisible jumps between fact and conclusion.
rituals.mission: Count the invisible jumps between fact and conclusion.
rituals.rule: Each unsupported leap counts as one step.
rituals.one_rule: Each unsupported leap counts as one step.
rituals.play: Use a mild example: FACT='They replied late.' CONCLUSION='They are angry with me.' Name every extra assumption needed to get from the fact to the conclusion and count them.
rituals.twist: Do not decide whether the conclusion is true; count only the bridge steps.
rituals.win: A conclusion becomes visibly separated from observation by its inference distance.
rituals.mindBend: The number of unsupported bridge steps between a fact and a conclusion makes inferential distance visible. This indicates how certainty can grow while evidence stays far away.
rituals.mind_bend: The number of unsupported bridge steps between a fact and a conclusion makes inferential distance visible. This indicates how certainty can grow while evidence stays far away.
rituals.safety: Use mild, ordinary evidence only. If interpretations become frightening or unverifiable, stop counting inference steps and check what is happening with a trusted person, clinician, or reliable external source.

rituals.name: CARRY-OFF SUM
rituals.unique_game_move: perform two-digit addition under a deliberately altered rule that forbids carrying between columns
rituals.recognition_cue: Mind play • Mental reset. ROUTER TAGS: creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility
rituals.immediate_need: restore flexible thinking

rituals.goal: Add numbers in a world where carrying is illegal.
rituals.mission: Add numbers in a world where carrying is illegal.
rituals.rule: In each column keep only the ones digit; every carry is discarded.
rituals.one_rule: In each column keep only the ones digit; every carry is discarded.
rituals.play: Add 58 + 67 with NO CARRY. Ones: 8+7=15, keep only 5 and discard the carry. Tens: 5+6=11, keep only 1. Read the altered-rule result.
rituals.twist: Compare the strange result with normal arithmetic only after finishing.
rituals.win: The altered-rule sum is 15, showing exactly how the no-carry system behaves.
rituals.mindBend: Two-digit addition produces a different result when carrying is forbidden. Arithmetic output is the consequence of the chosen algorithm, not the digits alone.
rituals.mind_bend: Two-digit addition produces a different result when carrying is forbidden. Arithmetic output is the consequence of the chosen algorithm, not the digits alone.
rituals.safety: Stay with neutral examples. When proof-seeking repetition becomes noticeable, stop and move on without forcing a solution.
